Name: -1_maiden_village_bride_servant
Representative_Docs:
['I had one and only son  
He hurried to live without a woman  
To manage without a partner.  
He started living, he started being,  
But he couldn't live without a woman  
Nor manage without a partner.  
He went from home to the courting path  
For a short time to the path of maidenhood.  
He came back home from courting,  
Then went to the back room,  
Put his hat on the table,  
Gloves on the edge of the hat,  
But himself started to cry.  
Then the father asked his son,  
"Why are you crying, young son?"  
"Why am I crying, dear father?  
I cannot live without a woman  
Nor manage without a partner.  
So I went briefly on the courting path  
For a short time on the maiden's way.  
The girls did not tolerate me  
They started to bark at me:  
'You don’t have a riffle shirt on,  
A riffle shirt, a silk vest,  
A cardaman at your neck,  
And German boots on your feet.'"  
Then the father understood and answered:  
"Don't cry, young son,  
Let's go to Riga to buy clothes,  
We'll buy you a riffle shirt,  
A riffle shirt, a silk vest,  
A cardaman to the neck,  
And German boots for your feet."  
"Then I went again on the courting path,  
For a short time on the maiden's way.  
The girls then loved me,  
They embraced me warmly,  
And kissed me sweetly.  
Then I came home from courting,  
I brought a wife to the house,  
Brought a daughter-in-law to the doorstep,  
Her chest was shining with jewelry,  
Her apron with proud lace."', "When I begin to compose poetry  
To sing poetry  
The whole village stays to listen  
The whole parish stays to watch  
My weary words  
A child's bad song  
Where did this child get those words  
From which words did they start  
She went to Harju to study  
To take a melody from Viru  
I heard, I answered back  
She did not go to Harju to study  
She did not go to Viru to take a melody  
In Harju studied the sisters  
In Viru the brother's wife  
They took, they took, the dear sisters  
They took me to a Viru man  
They made me beat my thigh  
Between five brothers  
At the hand of the sixth  
There my field became ruined  
My linen sack became sooty  
I went to the village to plow  
To borrow an ox from my father-in-law  
To steal some gold  
The villager took the ox to the village  
The father-in-law took the ox to the cellar  
The stolen goods to the chamber  
I took it and got angry  
I throw away my father-in-law’s shirt  
I throw away my mother-in-law’s shirt  
Immediately even my socks  
The villager brought the ox to the village  
The father-in-law brought it to the cellar  
The stolen goods to the chamber  
Wash well, maiden  
Wash well, fine one  
Make yourself white and clean.", 'Village boys, scythes at their belts,  
Young men, knives at their belts.  
My fiancé, buckle at his belt,  
My husband at Kalev's belt.  
Drinks a sip from the trough,  
Pulls toward the village's end,  
Down to the village mill.  
Throws the reins on the apple tree,  
The bridle in the linden tree.  
The riders in the blue cloak.  
Then he goes to look for the horse.  
Comes toward the maiden’s group,  
Driving the cattle at a distance.  
"Maiden, young man,  
Did you see my horse?"  
"Sweetheart, little brother,  
What color is your horse?  
Maybe I saw it, but I don’t know."  
"Maiden, young man,  
My horse is very beautiful:  
Golden-colored coat,  
Flaxen mane, leaf-shaped spots.  
Shackles on its feet,  
Golden bell on its neck,  
Silver bridle on its head,  
Copper bit in its mouth."  
"Sweetheart, little brother,  
That was your horse."  
Passed through our yard,  
Drank our river water,  
Tasted our sea water,  
Touched the village wells."  
"Come, come, young men,  
Come to the horse market,  
To listen to the golden bells."']
